role: 50th Vice President of the United States

documents.title: Hillbilly Elegy Tour Interviews, Columns & Messages (Charlie Rose, NPR, USA Today, NYT)
documents.source: PBS Charlie Rose / NPR / USA Today / New York Times
documents.text: I'm a Never Trump guy. I never liked him. Mr. Trump is unfit for our nation's highest office. Trump's actual policy proposals, such as they are, range from immoral to absurd. I'm going to vote third party because I can't stomach Trump. What Trump is doing is giving people an excuse to point the finger at someone else, point the finger at Mexican immigrants, or Chinese trade, or the Democratic elites, or whatever else. Trump is cultural heroin. He makes some feel better for a bit, but he cannot fix what ails them, and one day they'll realize it. Trump makes people I care about afraid. Immigrants, Muslims, etc. Because of this I find him reprehensible. In the 2017 Republican healthcare repeal bill, millions will be unable to pay for basic health care. Republicans find themselves mired in internal contradictions, arguing that a bill that cuts subsidies for the poor somehow makes care more accessible. Those folks who voted for Donald Trump will lose out most. Trump has just so thoroughly failed to deliver on his economic populism, excepting a disjointed China policy.

documents.title: Fox News Q&A, New Right Podcasts & Postliberal Panel
documents.source: Tucker Carlson Tonight / Jack Murphy Live / Catholic University Panel
documents.text: We are effectively run in this country, via the Democrats, via our corporate oligarchs, by a bunch of childless cat ladies who are miserable at their own lives and the choices that they've made, and so they want to make the rest of the country miserable too. It's just a basic fact. You look at Kamala Harris, Pete Buttigieg, AOC, the entire future of the Democrats is controlled by people without children. And how does it make any sense that we've turned our country over to people that don't have a direct stake in it? I identify as a member of the postliberal right, and I see my role in Congress as explicitly anti-regime. I think what Trump should do, if I was giving him one piece of advice: fire every single mid-level bureaucrat, every civil servant in the administrative state, replace them with our people. And when the courts stop you, stand before the country like Andrew Jackson did and say the chief justice has made his ruling, now let him enforce it.

documents.title: 2024 Republican National Convention Vice Presidential Acceptance Speech
documents.text: Greetings, Milwaukee, my fellow Americans and my fellow Republicans. My name is JD Vance from the great state of Ohio. Tonight is a night of hope, a celebration of what America once was, and with God's grace, what it will soon be again. For the last eight years, President Trump has given everything he has to fight for the people of our country. He didn't need politics, but the country needed him. That's the Republican Party of the next four years, united in our love for this country and committed to free speech and the open exchange of ideas. Never in my wildest imagination could I have believed that I'd be standing here tonight. I grew up in Middletown, Ohio, a small town where people spoke their minds, built with their hands and loved their God, their family, their community and their country with their whole hearts. But it was also a place that had been cast aside and forgotten by America's ruling class in Washington. When I was in the fourth grade, a career politician by the name of Joe Biden supported NAFTA, a bad trade deal that sent countless good jobs to Mexico. When I was a sophomore in high school, that same career politician named Joe Biden gave China a sweetheart trade deal that destroyed even more good American middle class manufacturing jobs. When I was a senior in high school, that same Joe Biden supported the disastrous invasion of Iraq, and at each step of the way in small towns like mine in Ohio or next door in Pennsylvania or Michigan, jobs were sent overseas and our children were sent to war. Our country was flooded with cheap Chinese goods, with cheap foreign labor, and in the decades to come, deadly Chinese fentanyl. Joe Biden screwed up, and my community paid the price. Mamaw raised me as my mother struggled with addiction. After 9/11 I enlisted in the United States Marines, went to Ohio State University, and went to Yale Law School. My work taught me that there is still so much talent and grit in the American heartland. For these places to thrive, we need a leader who fights for the people who built this country. We need a leader who's not in the pocket of big business but answers to the working man, union and non-union alike. A leader who won't sell out to multinational corporations, but will stand up for American companies and American industry. A leader who rejects Joe Biden and Kamala Harris's green new scam and fights to bring back our great American factories. As always, America's ruling class wrote the checks; communities like mine paid the price. For decades, that divide between the few with their power and comfort in Washington and the rest of us only widened. A country where a working class boy born far from the halls of power can stand on this stage as the next Vice President of the United States of America. It's about the auto worker in Michigan, the factory worker in Wisconsin, the energy worker in Pennsylvania and Ohio, single moms like mine who struggled with money and addiction, grandparents living on Social Security. Donald Trump reversed decades of betrayals inflicted by Joe Biden and the rest of the corrupt Washington insiders. He created the greatest economy in history for workers. Workers' wages went through the roof. Wall Street barons crashed the economy, and American builders went out of business. Then the Democrats flooded this country with millions of illegal aliens, so citizens had to compete with people who shouldn't even be here for precious housing. Joe Biden's inflation crisis is really an affordability crisis, and many of the people that I grew up with can't afford to pay more for groceries, more for gas, more for rent. China and the cartels sent fentanyl across the border. We're done catering to Wall Street; we'll commit to the working man. We're done importing foreign labor. We're going to fight for American citizens and their good jobs and their good wages. We're done buying energy from countries that hate us. We're done sacrificing supply chains to unlimited global trade, and we're going to stamp more and more products with that beautiful label Made in the USA. We're going to build factories again, put people to work making real products for American families made with the hands of American workers. Together, we will protect the wages of American workers and stop the Chinese Communist Party from building their middle class on the backs of American citizens. Together, we will make sure our allies share in the burden of securing world peace, no more free rides for nations that betray the generosity of the American taxpayer. Together, we will send our kids to war only when we must. America is not just an idea. It is a group of people with a shared history and a common future. It is a nation. When we allow newcomers into our American family, we allow them on our terms. People will not fight for abstractions, they will fight for their home. That is our homeland.

documents.title: CNN State of the Union Q&A with Dana Bash on Springfield, Ohio
documents.source: CNN State of the Union Transcript
documents.text: Dana, the evidence is the firsthand account of my constituents who are telling me that this happened. I've been trying to talk about the problems in Springfield for months and the American media ignored it. The American media totally ignored this stuff until Donald Trump and I started talking about cat memes. If I have to create stories so that the American media actually pays attention to the suffering of the American people, then that's what I'm going to do, Dana, because you guys are completely letting Kamala Harris coast. I say that we're creating a story, meaning we're creating the American media focusing on it. We didn't create 20,000 illegal migrants coming into Springfield thanks to Kamala Harris's policies. Her policies did that, but yes, we created the actual focus that allowed the American media to talk about this story and the suffering caused by Kamala Harris's policies.

documents.title: CBS News Vice Presidential Debate vs. Gov. Tim Walz
documents.text: So, Margaret, I want to answer the question. First of all, thanks, Governor, thanks to CBS, and thanks most importantly to the American people. I was raised in a working-class family. My mother required food assistance for periods of her life. My grandmother required Social Security help to raise me because my own mother struggled with addiction. I went to college on the GI Bill after I enlisted in the Marine Corps and served in Iraq. I know that a lot of you are worried about the chaos in the world and the feeling that the American Dream is unattainable. If we get Donald Trump back in the White House, the American Dream is going to be attainable once again. Donald Trump actually delivered stability in the world by establishing effective deterrence. Peace through strength. Margaret, my point is that we already have massive child separations thanks to Kamala Harris's open border. She enabled the Mexican drug cartels to operate freely in this country, and they use children as drug mules. Look, I think what Tim said just doesn't pass the smell test. The only thing that she did when she became the appointed border czar was to undo 94 Donald Trump executive actions that opened the border. Look, Margaret, first of all, the gross majority of what we need to do at the southern border is just empowering law enforcement to do their job. Look, in Springfield, Ohio and in communities all across this country, you've got schools that are overwhelmed, hospitals that are overwhelmed, housing that is totally unaffordable because we brought in millions of illegal immigrants to compete with Americans for scarce homes. Margaret, the rules were that you guys weren't going to fact check, and since you're fact checking me, I think it's important to say what's actually going on. There's an application called the CBP One app where you can go on as an illegal migrant, apply for asylum or parole and be granted legal status at the wave of a Kamala Harris open border wand. Well, first of all, you're going to hear a lot from Tim Walz, and some of it, I'll be honest with you, even sounds pretty good. A lot of those same economists attack Donald Trump's plans, and they have PhDs, but they don't have common sense and they don't have wisdom, because Donald Trump's economic policies delivered the highest take-home pay in a generation. I know a lot of you are struggling. It's going to stop when Donald Trump brings back common sense to this country. Governor, you say trust the experts, but those same experts for 40 years said that if we shipped our manufacturing base off to China, we'd get cheaper goods. They lied about that. They were wrong about that. We're not going to stop it by listening to experts. We're going to stop it by listening to common sense wisdom. I was raised by a woman who would sometimes go into medical debt so that she could put food on the table. We just got to get back to common sense economic principles. Well, first of all, Margaret, I've been extremely open about the fact that I was wrong about Donald Trump. I was wrong because I believed some of the media stories that turned out to be dishonest fabrications of his record. Donald Trump delivered rising wages, rising take-home pay, an economy that worked for normal Americans, a secure southern border. If you're trying to employ slave laborers in China at three dollars a day, you're going to undercut the wages of American workers. I want us as a Republican Party to be pro-family in the fullest sense of the word. Twenty-five million illegal aliens competing with Americans for scarce homes is one of the most significant drivers of home prices in the country. Well, there's a Federal Reserve study that we're happy to share after the debate, we'll put it up on social media. Look, we are a country of builders, doers, explorers, but we have a regulatory regime of Kamala Harris. I think this concepts of a plan remark is very simple common sense. You're not going to propose a 900-page bill standing on a debate stage. When Obamacare was crushing under the weight of its own regulatory burden, Donald Trump could have destroyed the program; instead he salvaged Obamacare and worked in a bipartisan way. Well, Norah, first of all, I think that we're focused on the future. Remember, he said on January 6th the protesters ought to protest peacefully, and on January 20th Donald Trump peacefully gave over power. We actually do have a threat to democracy in this country, and it is the threat of censorship. Kamala Harris is engaged in censorship at an industrial scale. I remember when I was being raised by my grandmother when she didn't have enough money to turn on the heat some nights. Whether you're rich or poor, you ought to be able to afford a nice meal for your family, afford to buy a house, live in safe neighborhoods, not have your communities flooded with fentanyl.

documents.title: 61st Munich Security Conference Address
documents.text: One of the things that I wanted to talk about today is, of course, our shared values. While the Trump administration is very concerned with European security and believes that we can come to a reasonable settlement between Russia and Ukraine, and that Europe must step up in a big way to provide for its own defense, the threat that I worry the most about vis-a-vis Europe is not Russia, it's not China, it's not any other external actor. What I worry about is the threat from within, the retreat of Europe from some of its most fundamental values, values shared with the United States of America. When we see European courts canceling elections and senior officials threatening to cancel others, we ought to ask whether we're holding ourselves to an appropriately high standard. In Britain and across Europe, free speech, I fear, is in retreat. Sometimes the loudest voices for censorship have come not from within Europe but from within my own country, where the prior administration threatened and bullied social media companies to censor so-called misinformation. In Washington, there is a new sheriff in town. Under Donald Trump's leadership, we may disagree with your views, but we will fight to defend your right to offer it in the public square. Old, entrenched interests are hiding behind ugly Soviet-era words like misinformation and disinformation simply because they don't like the idea that someone with an alternative viewpoint might express a different opinion, vote a different way, or win an election. There is no security if you are afraid of the voices, opinions, and conscience that guide your very own people. The crisis this continent faces right now is one of our own making. If you're running in fear of your own voters, there is nothing America can do for you. You cannot win a democratic mandate by censoring opponents, jailing them, or ignoring voters on key issues like mass migration. No voter opened the floodgates to millions of unvetted immigrants. There is no room for firewalls. People care about their homes, dreams, safety, and future.

documents.title: Oval Office Zelenskyy Exchange, Senate Tie-Breakers & 2025-2026 Economic Tour
documents.source: White House Pool / C-SPAN / Public Statements
documents.text: The path to peace and the path to prosperity is maybe engaging in diplomacy. What makes America a good country is America engaging in diplomacy. Have you said thank you once? In this entire meeting, have you said thank you? Judges aren't allowed to control the executive's legitimate power. Pete Hegseth is a disrupter, and a lot of people don't like that disruption. Think about all those bipartisan massive votes: what did they get us? We fought many wars over the last 40 years, but haven't won a war about as long as I've been alive. Unless you're willing to use American power and tariffs to fight back against foreign countries that use slave labor to undercut the wages of American workers, you are never going to rebuild American manufacturing. Everything else — the CBO score, the proper baseline, the minutiae of the Medicaid policy — is immaterial compared to the ICE money and immigration enforcement provisions. Flood the country with illegal immigration and give migrants generous benefits, and that will bankrupt the country. Here's what the One Big Beautiful Bill means for you: take-home pay is going to go up, probably seven or eight thousand dollars per family over the next three to four years. If you build or expand a great American factory, the federal government is going to reward you. We've got to take America's streets back for the American people. You earned it, you ought to keep it, and we ought to keep our hands the hell out of your pocket in Washington, D.C. We're going to put a big, fat tariff on those foreign companies bringing that stuff into the United States. After the first year of President Donald Trump's leadership, we are rebuilding the American Dream, and we are taking back this country.
